title: Introduce RAG batched-tool sandbox and notebook playground
author: Sofia Park
release_notes: Adds an interactive RAG sandbox demonstrating batched tool-calls, streaming tool output examples, and a notebook-playground with smoke tests. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: provide a compact, opinionated example that demonstrates how to safely batch tool-calls in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) flows on Redwood, while preserving streaming responsiveness and predictable unit economics. This sandbox is intended for engineers evaluating batching trade-offs (latency vs cost), authoring tool contracts, and validating streaming partial results inside notebooks.

This PR introduces: 1) a sandbox runner that executes RAG sessions with configurable batch windows and a mock tool registry that supports both sync and streaming tool protocols; 2) a Jupyter/Colab-friendly notebook that walks through the lifecycle (index -> query -> tool-call batching -> streaming aggregation -> result normalization); 3) TypeScript and Python example bindings for the sandbox runner so teams can copy/paste into their projects; 4) a minimal e2e smoke harness that runs the sandbox locally in CI; 5) docs and a short tutorial in the examples README describing when to use batching and common pitfalls.

Checklist:
- [x] Add sandbox runner and tool registry (ts/python)
- [x] Notebook walkthrough with stepwise assertions
- [x] Samples showing batched vs unbatched metrics (latency/cost)
- [x] CI smoke test that verifies no regressions in sandbox runner
- [x] Docs and README + quickstart command
- [x] Code comments and lightweight diagrams in README

Testing notes: CI runs the smoke harness that starts a lightweight mocked Redis cache and spawns the sandbox with three simulated tool providers (fast, slow-stream, batched-worker). The harness asserts that: 1) batched requests reduce total token count to simulated model backend by >=12% in the example workload; 2) streaming tools surface partial payloads within 300ms after tool-worker emits first chunk; 3) fallbacks to unbatched path occur cleanly if the batch window is exceeded. CI initially flaked on the streaming integration due to timing assumptions (see review comments), fixed by increasing mock tool backpressure timeouts and adding jitter-resilient assertions.

Usage: 'examples/rag-batched-sandbox/README.md' contains quickstart commands; the notebook lives at 'examples/rag-batched-sandbox/notebooks/batched_tool_demo.ipynb'. The TypeScript sample is 'examples/rag-batched-sandbox/ts-client' and Python sample is 'examples/rag-batched-sandbox/py-client'.

Notes on design decisions: the sandbox opts for an explicit batch window (configurable in ms) instead of implicit rate heuristics to keep the example easy to reason about. Tool-call bundling is demonstrated using a deterministic keying scheme (by tool and input-shard) to make it straightforward to map batched responses back to original requests. The streaming tool adapter uses chunked JSON-lines over a small websocket shim to remain implementation-agnostic for both hosted and private deployments.

Related work: this ties to ENG-2146 (inference batching policy RFC) and the 'streaming partial results' doc in the runtime folder.
